newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Anwar asks ministers to stop squabbling.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Anwar asks ministers to stop squabbling.

text.p: Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has warned Malaysia's Cabinet members against sniping about each other's ministries in public, the national Bernama news agency said on Tuesday.
He said while the ministers have the right to comment on each other's departments, they should do so through either the prime minister, himself or the Cabinet.

"Our tradition and culture dictate that when there are problems affecting other ministries, the minister concerned should go through the Prime Minister, me or the Cabinet," Anwar was quoted as saying after opening the 1996 annual meeting of the Malaysian Crime Prevention Foundation.
Anwar was responding to questions about an ongoing feud between National Unity and Social Development Minister Zaleha Ismail and the Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Abdul Rahim Noor.
Zaleha had accused the police of being apathetic about complaints of domestic violence, which Abdul Rahim has denied.
Anwar said he has ordered the two to end their quarrel and stop making statements in the media.

"I'm not questioning the issue raised but I am also the acting Home Minister. By right they should have referred to me so that I can ask the IGP for explanation or bring it direct to the Cabinet," Anwar was quoted by Bernama as saying.
Anwar said he raised the issue of quarrelsome ministers at last week's Cabinet meeting and was able to persuade them to tone down their public bickering.
"I stressed that one minister should not touch the decision of another on his job. He can only give his views at Cabinet meetings," he said.
The local media has recently reported several tiffs between Cabinet members.

Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik was quoted in newspapers as saying some funds were missing from the Rubber Industry Smallholders Development Agency, drawing a strong reaction from Rural Development Minister Annuar Musa.
Lim later denied he made the allegation and blamed the media for misquoting him.

Also recently, Domestic Trade and Consumer Affairs Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob had a run-in with Health Minister Chua Jui Meng over the amount of imitation medicines in circulation within Malaysia.
